entry.title: The Origin Of Eric Wind's Jaeger-LeCoultre Reverso Engraving

media:group.media:title: The Origin Of Eric Wind's Jaeger-LeCoultre Reverso Engraving
media:group.media:description:
Eric's Reverso Tribute to 1931 U.S. Edition was a wedding gift from his friend Jack Carlson and has been a faithful companion ever since. More recently, Eric had the caseback engraved with Our Lady of Guadalupe, a choice connected to his faith and to discoveries about his father's Mexican family. The engraving came with one unwelcome surprise: the case was polished during the process. We'll let the video detail Eric's spirited reaction to the service.

entry.title: Why The Rolex 5512 Is Always A Classic Watch

media:group.media:title: Why The Rolex 5512 Is Always A Classic Watch
media:group.media:description:
If Eric Wind had to choose one watch, his Rolex Submariner Reference 5512 would be a serious contender. His example is a four-line, meters-first watch with the rare dial variation collectors call 'Neat Fonts.' It is the unpolished vintage Submariner he had hoped to find after years of looking, and it previously appeared in Hodinkee's Reference Points on the Submariner.
Charlie Dunne's own meters-first 5512 began as a loan. He asked to borrow it for a Thanksgiving drive home to Ponte Vedra Beach and found himself enamored with the way it wore. When he returned, Eric told him the watch was his. It became Charlie's first vintage Rolex and helped turn his interest in Submariners into a deeper study of the differences between the chronometer-rated 5512 and the 5513.

entry.title: Why Vintage Domino's Rolexes Actually Exist

media:group.media:title: Why Vintage Domino's Rolexes Actually Exist
media:group.media:description:
Eric Wind often travels with this 34mm Air-King because of its simplicity and versatility. As Eric explains in the episode, qualifying Domino's franchisees or managers could receive a Rolex after meeting a sales target for three consecutive weeks. His example carries the recipient's initials and those of Domino's founder Tom Monaghan on the caseback, along with a clasp engraved by the retailer during a brief period in the early 1990s.

entry.title: Talking Watches: Rare Rolex, Patek, Cartier, & More With Eric Wind And Charlie Dunne

media:group.media:title: Talking Watches: Rare Rolex, Patek, Cartier, & More With Eric Wind And Charlie Dunne
media:group.media:description:
Vintage-watch experts Eric Wind and Charlie Dunne join Hodinkee for a special episode of Talking Watches, marking the first time Ben has welcomed two guests to the table.
Eric was one of Hodinkee’s earliest contributors and later became a specialist at Christie’s before founding Wind Vintage. Charlie began as a collector and researcher, eventually turning an internship with Eric into a career working alongside him.
The watches they brought reflect that history. Highlights include a pair of Rolex Submariner Reference 5512s, an exceptional rose-gold Patek Philippe Reference 2508, and two deeply personal Jaeger-LeCoultre alarm watches. We also see a platinum Cartier Tank Normale NSO, an Enicar Sherpa Ultradive, rare pocket watches, and an early preview of an unreleased Bamford Carrera created with Eric.
Throughout the episode, Eric and Charlie discuss condition, the watches they have given each other, and the shared obsession that became their profession. They also introduce their new book, Vintage Watches: The Modern Guide.
Watch the full episode and discover what two of the vintage world’s most respected voices keep for themselves.
